primitives.name: Possession Retention Tradeoff
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this work, we specifically evaluate the trade-off between trying to retain possession versus intentionally putting the ball out of play near the opponentʼs goal for a throw-in.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_{retention}': 'probability of retaining possession', 'P_{throwin}': 'probability of scoring from opponent throw-in'}
primitives.assumptions: Players act rationally under uncertainty; game state is Markovian.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When possession loss risk exceeds throw-in scoring potential.

layer2.mapping: GSI computes posterior P(score|throw-in) via ML; GSE evaluates transition from defensive to offensive states.
layer2.telemetry: Expected goal value difference between pass and throw-in.

primitives.name: Throw-In Scoring Probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Regularly you see teams employing it as a kick-off strategy.<sup>1</sup> The underlying belief is that an opponent throw-in in the corner of the pitch is worth more than established possession in the center of the pitch.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_{score}(x)': 'probability of scoring given throw-in at position x'}
primitives.assumptions: Throw-in location affects scoring likelihood; opponent pressure is modeled as binary.

layer2.mapping: GSI maps p_{score}(x) to expected value function; GSE uses it for policy selection in high-risk zones.
layer2.telemetry: Observed goal rate per throw-in bin.

primitives.name: Backward Pass Risk Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: First, professional players should consistently be able to clear the ball out of play near the final third from the midfield area.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{pass}': 'risk of losing possession via backward pass', 'R_{throw}': 'risk of losing possession via throw-in'}
primitives.assumptions: Passes toward own goal increase turnover risk; throw-ins are less risky near opponent’s goal.

layer2.mapping: GSI quantifies R_{pass} using ML classification of pass angles; GSE models risk as state transition cost.
layer2.telemetry: Pass angle distribution vs. possession retention rate.

The Boot It principle formalizes this through a stochastic decision process where the expected value of a throw-in (E[V_{throw}]) is compared against E[V_{pass}] under similar conditions. The model assumes that the probability of scoring from a throw-in increases with proximity to the opponent's goal, as seen in Table 1. This leads to a dual optimization problem: minimizing risk of possession loss while maximizing scoring opportunities. The failure mode occurs when players misjudge the spatial context, leading to suboptimal decisions in high-pressure scenarios. The mathematical structure resembles a Markov Decision Process with reward functions defined over spatial bins.
